skill.name: smc-chart-analysis
skill.description: Analyzes markets with Smart Money Concepts and ICT methodology using a local chart API. It identifies bias, liquidity, fair value gaps, entries, stops, targets, and risk warnings.

content.value_statement: Traders need structured SMC analysis without manually checking every liquidity level. This skill converts local chart data into bias, entries, stops, targets, and risk warnings.
actual_capabilities: Fetches mechanical SMC data from a local `localhost:3001` API when that service is running.
Reviews market structure, liquidity pools, fair value gaps, structure breaks, and ATR.
Builds a directional trade setup with entry zone, stop loss, targets, and risk-to-reward context.
Grades setups from A+ to C based on bias, confluence, timing, and price location.
Formats results with warnings, confluence factors, and a short market narrative.
limitations: Requires the separate local web app and API; the skill does not include that service.
The documented symbol examples focus on BTC, ETH, and SOL.
Outputs are market analysis, not financial advice or guaranteed signals.
SMC and ICT interpretations can be subjective and should be checked against other evidence.

use_cases.title: Crypto Setup Review
use_cases.description: Review BTC, ETH, or SOL before planning a discretionary trade.

use_cases.title: Chart Research Notes
use_cases.description: Convert mechanical SMC data into consistent notes for a watchlist.

use_cases.title: Methodology Teaching
use_cases.description: Show how liquidity, premium or discount zones, and fair value gaps support a trade thesis.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze BTC/USDT on the 1h timeframe using the SMC workflow. Include bias, setup grade, entry zone, stop loss, targets, and warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Entry Timeframes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze BTC/USDT with 4h bias and 15m entry context. Explain where liquidity, FVGs, and structure breaks align or conflict.

prompt_templates.title: Grade a Watchlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, and SOL/USDT for intraday SMC setups. Rank them by confluence and explain which setups to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test a Thesis
prompt_templates.prompt: I am considering a long setup on ETH/USDT. Use SMC data to challenge the thesis, list invalidation levels, and identify safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: Analyze BTC/USDT on 1h for an intraday setup.
output_examples.output: A structured SMC note with directional bias, setup grade, entry zone, stop, targets, confluence checklist, warnings, and narrative.
A multi-timeframe explanation that separates higher-timeframe bias from lower-timeframe entry timing and highlights conflicts.

output_examples.input: Rank BTC, ETH, and SOL for SMC opportunities.
output_examples.output: A watchlist summary that prioritizes symbols by confluence and marks weak setups as wait or avoid.

best_practices: Confirm the local API is running before asking for analysis.
Ask for specific symbol, timeframe, and trading style.
Treat every setup as a hypothesis and define invalidation before entry.
anti_patterns: Using the output as a guaranteed trading signal.
Requesting broad market calls without a symbol or timeframe.
Ignoring the warning section when the setup grade is weak.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It only analyzes chart data and formats trade setup notes.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: The documented workflow calls a local API at localhost:3001. Any market data access depends on that separate service.

faq.question: Can it analyze stocks or forex?
faq.answer: It can analyze any market that the local API supports. The included examples focus on crypto symbols.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides educational market analysis and should not replace independent risk management.

faq.question: What methods does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Smart Money Concepts and ICT-style ideas, including liquidity sweeps, fair value gaps, order blocks, and market structure.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple timeframes?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports higher-timeframe bias and lower-timeframe entry context when the API can provide both.
